To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bovine peripheral blood lymphocyte responses to proteins of Brucell abortus can be determined by using protein immunoblots.
bovine lymphocyte proliferative responses to Brucella abortusspecific antigens can be determined by using protein immunoblots.
bovine PBM cells respond to extracted B. abortus proteins by proliferating and that the responding cells are specific only to proteins of corresponding molecular sizes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of Brucellae antigens which are important to cellular responses.
the identification of Brucellae antigenic determinants and their role in cellular responses.
identifying and characterizing Brucella antigens important in the immune response to vaccination with live B. abortus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bovine PBM cells respond to individual B. abortus proteins of high, medium, and low molecular weights.
the bovine PBM cells respond to proteins of B. abortus and that the responses are specific to individual proteins.
the bovine PBM cell proliferative response to B. abortus proteins blotted onto a nitrocellulode membrane is antigen specific and is dependent on the presence of the protein on the nitrocellulodse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bovine immune response to the B. abortus vaccine strain 19 is directed toward a number of proteins, including those of high, medium and low molecular weight.
the cellular response to B. abortus proteins is not a response to the lipopolysacharide or other carbohydrate, but to the proteins of molecular weights greater than 45, 000.
the protein immunoblot technique is an effective method for identifying and characterizing Brucella antigen(s) important in cellular responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of protein immunoblots to study cellular responses to individual bacterial proteins is a useful tool in the study of the cellular immune response to Brucella abortu
it is possible to study the cellular immune responses of cattle to specific Brucella antigens without cloning the bacterial gene or purifying the specific antigen.
the cellular response to Brucella is a complex one and that there is a lot of work ahead of us.
